method: Mouse interaction and visual inspection of the actual native GUI through Windows Computer Use
tested_build: GUI prototype before the final executable and window/class rename

checks.name: Green and cream board, shadowed pieces, coordinates, readable sidebar
Selecting e2 shows e3 and e4 legal move dots
Selecting another friendly piece replaces move hints
Capture marker on d5 and e4xd5 board update
e2e4 d7d5 f1b5 displays Check and red king; c7c6 clears it
Friend game f2f3 e7e5 g2g4 d8h4 displays Checkmate
Easy mode starts a new game and replies to e2e4
Medium mode starts a new game and replies to e2e4
Hard mode starts a new game and replies to e2e4
Switching back to Friend starts a local two-player game
Restart restores initial position and White turn
Promotion selector changes to N and back to Q

notes: These interaction checks were performed on the 4,935-byte GUI prototype. The final 4,932-byte chess5kb.exe was rebuilt after changing the window title and registered window class name to chess5kb. It shares the tested chess core and GUI behavior, but it is not byte-identical to the tested prototype. Separate release build checks verify the final file size, SHA-256, x86 GUI PE headers, and retained relocation data; see release.json. The core's separate 34-scenario report includes actual N/B/R/Q promotion execution for both colors. GUI promotion selection was tested separately.
